title: Scoring one key against three nodes
request:
three nodes, the whole ranking for one key, then the plain lookup

./your_program.sh rendezvous
add n1
add n2
add n3
locate-k user-42 3
locate user-42
note: `locate` is not a second implementation. It is `locate-k <key> 1` with the brackets taken off, and the suite checks exactly that: a head that disagrees with the ranking means two different score functions are in the program.

title: A node leaves
request:
the ranking for a key, then the same ranking without `n1`

./your_program.sh rendezvous
add n1
add n2
add n3
locate-k user-42 3
remove n1
locate-k user-42 3
locate user-42
note: This is what rendezvous buys over a ring: not only do the survivors keep their keys, the *replicas* keep their order, so a key whose owner died already knows which node takes over without asking anybody.
